sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F8][F145], while operating income grew faster at 9.9% [F146] and net income barely moved at 0.4% [F147].
The window is not a smooth compounder: operating margin swung from 30.6% in FY2019 to 15.5% in FY2021, then to 41.3% in FY2023 and back to 32.1% in FY2025 [F18][F20][F22][F24].
The FY2021 collapse reflected a $1.5 billion Mountain Valley Pipeline impairment and unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity at NEER [P63][P68].
The FY2023 spike came from $1,729 million of non-qualifying hedge gains in NEER's net income [P30], and FY2024 revenue fell 5.2% on lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues at FPL [D201][P35].
FPL remains the largest revenue source at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271], contributing 5.5pp of the 9.8% revenue growth [D273][D236].
FPL's FY2025 revenue rose $1,243 million on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
NEER's net income rose to $2,975 million in FY2025 from $2,299 million in FY2024 [S28][S29], while FPL earned $5,012 million against $4,543 million [P23].
NEER's increase came from new wind, solar and battery investments, partly offset by higher financing costs [P26][P13].
Operating income grew 10.7% against 9.8% revenue growth in FY2025 [D237][D236], but diluted EPS fell 2.1% [D240] as the share count rose 0.6% [D251].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sits 1.8pp above the 30.3% window median and well below the 41.3% FY2023 high [F24][D300][D299].
The FY2025 margin was essentially flat, up 0.3pp [D247], as operating expenses grew 10.0% against 9.8% revenue growth [D249][D236].
Depreciation and amortization rose $951 million, mainly higher amortization of deferred storm costs from Hurricanes Debby, Helene and Milton [P16].
Below the line, other income (expense) was -$3,750 million [X64], driven by non-qualifying interest rate hedge losses and higher average debt balances at Corporate and Other [P8].
A -17.7% effective tax rate [D226], reflecting clean energy tax credits [P11], kept net margin at 26.5% [F40], below the 32.1% operating margin [F24].
Operating cash flow of $12,485 million was 1.83x net income in FY2025 [F64][F32][D227], in line with the 1.55x to 2.73x range of prior years [D157][D52].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% [D241] and was 48.4% of revenue [D225], while investing outflow reached $23,865 million [F72].
The swing from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
D&A of $6,580 million [X32] far exceeds reported capex embedded in the investing outflow, so capital intensity is funded largely through debt rather than internal cash.
Total debt reached $95,011 million in FY2025 against $2,812 million of cash, a net debt position of $92,199 million [D230][D229][D231].
Net cash is -357.4% of revenue [D232], the 0th percentile against utilities peers whose median is -228.4% [D314][D315].
Long-term debt grew 23.7% in FY2025 [D245] on $23,394 million of issuance against $10,347 million of repayment [X90][X98].
Free cash flow was consumed by $4,680 million of dividends [X82][D233], and the diluted share count still rose 0.6% [D251], so capital return did not offset dilution.
The current ratio is 0.60x in FY2025 [F128], below 1.0x, though it is the window high [D305] and typical for a utility funding construction with short-term debt.
Net cash has fallen for seven straight years, from -$34,325 million in FY2018 to -$92,199 million in FY2025 [D9][D231], as debt growth outran cash generation.
The FY2025 effective tax rate moved -23.3pp to -17.7% [D226][D191], reflecting clean energy tax credits that lower reported taxes but are non-cash [P11].
FY2019 operating expenses were later restated to $14,257 million from $13,851 million [X18][R5], a data-quality caveat on that year's margin comparison.
Watch operating margin against the 30.3% window median [D300]: a print below it in the FY2026 10-K would reverse the FY2025 stabilisation.
Watch net cash against the FY2025 level of -$92,199 million [D231]: further deterioration would extend the seven-year trend of rising leverage.
Watch operating cash flow against the FY2025 1.83x conversion of net income [D227]: a drop toward the FY2018 0.99x [D5] would signal weaker earnings quality.
